reviewEvidence: Third pass, on the repair revision. PASS 1 (verify) re-checked every acceptance criterion against the code and reproduced both RED claims by stashing source. PASS 2 was an independent adversarial review by a fresh-context agent with no memory of the implementation, told to falsify the two strongest claims, check each AC against code rather than tests, sweep for regressions from the two deleted registry fields, and run the security profile; it verified the security surface clean (no dependency changes, fixed installer argv, unchanged confirm/hasUI gate, audit redaction covering the new failure paths, diagnostics reaching only the operator UI) and the regression sweep clean, but falsified the broader "no path drops stderr" claim and surfaced eight further gaps. PASS 3 is this repair: all thirteen findings were fixed under TDD (each slice began with a test whose RED output is the defect itself — `'Failed to spawn: devcontainer'` without the errno, `'host-out\n'` without `--- stderr ---`, `'docker remove failed with exit 1.'` without the daemon message, `'container out\n'` without the container's stderr half, `'npm install exited null'` instead of the signal, an undefined `errorSummary` on the non-zero-exit and failed-probe records, `'supersecret-token-value'` returned unredacted, `expected true to be false` for a sub-millisecond timeout that aborted at 0 ms, and `displayCommandResult is not a function`), and one further defect was found while fixing them: `/devcontainer <verb>` produced no output at all, because Pi's command dispatcher ignores a handler's return value (`_tryExecuteExtensionCommand` is `return await command.handler(args, ctx), true`) and nothing rendered `CommandResult.text`. Verification of the repair: `npm run typecheck`; `npm run test:unit` (31 files, 344 tests, 23 added by this repair); `verify-package.mjs --unit-tests` (all gates); a rebuilt and committed `dist/` that matches a fresh build; the packed `smoke-pi-package.mjs --no-model`; and `npm run install:local -- --check`. The Dev Containers CLI contract was re-confirmed against the version this host actually resolves, 0.89.0: every flag the adapter passes (`up`/`build`/`exec`, `--workspace-folder`, `--docker-path`, `--config`, `--container-id`, `--remote-env`) still exists in the installed help output, so the 0.88.0 pin documented in the repository remains conservative rather than wrong. Two seams remain outside unit-test reach and are reported as such rather than claimed covered: the delivery of a command handler's rendered result and the drain of discovery diagnostics both live in the extension's command dispatch, which this repository has no unit harness for (the same limitation the Phase 1 review recorded); their policy halves are unit-tested (`displayCommandResult`, `reportDiscoveryDiagnostics`) and the wiring is exercised by the packed smoke run. The previous revision's approval was withdrawn when the repair landed (recorded below as a note) and is restored here against revision-99abdc7f.

findings.message: FIXED. `toSpawnError` named no errno for anything other than ENOENT/EACCES/EPERM, so a host-side transport failure (`ENOTCONN` from a half-dead filesystem mount sitting in PATH, which makes glibc's execvp abort the whole search) was indistinguishable from a missing binary — the misdiagnosis this phase is about. Every branch now carries the code, and ENOTCONN gets its own message and remedy. Verified by four new unit tests that call the mapper directly, and by the `docs/troubleshooting.md` entry describing the symptom, the cause and the one-line fix. Not previously introduced by this phase; it is the reason the phase's own goal failed in the field.

FIXED. AC-2 was satisfied as worded (it names `devcontainer_exec`, and the host tool was fixed with it), but the L2-02 class was not closed repo-wide. Now closed: `/devcontainer host-exec` (the command surface) uses the shared combiner; `docker logs` captures the container's stderr half — `grep -c onStderr src/runtime/docker-lifecycle.ts` was 0 before this repair and the adapter returned only the stdout half of every log read; and `stop`/`remove` failures carry a bounded, flattened one-line rendering of what Docker actually said instead of only the exit code. Verified by three new tests (command surface mixed streams, logs with both streams, destructive failure carrying the daemon message), each shown RED first.

FIXED. `Math.round(seconds * 1000)` turned a positive sub-millisecond timeout into `setTimeout(..., 0)`, i.e. an immediate abort reported as a timeout — the failure `exclusiveMinimum: 0` cannot express. Both entry points (`src/tools.ts` and the routed bash router, which takes Pi's own unbounded `timeout`) now go through one `resolveTimeoutMs` that floors at 1 ms, and sub-second deadlines render in milliseconds rather than as `timed out after 0s`. Verified by fake-timer tests at both layers that advance virtual time by 0 ms and assert the promise has NOT settled, then by 1 ms and assert the typed timeout — the RED for which was literally `expected true to be false`.

FIXED. A signal-killed install resolves with `exitCode: null`, and the result read `npm install exited null`, discarding the one field that says what happened. The failure now names the signal (and appends any captured stderr), and the audit record carries the same text as its error summary.

FIXED. The record was written for the install stage before the verification probe, so a failed probe left `exitCode: 0` with no error summary in the trail while the operator was told `[setup-failed]`. The record is now written once, after the outcome is known, carrying the failure reason as its error summary — one attempt, one record, and the record says how the attempt ended. Verified by a test that fails a probe and asserts exactly one record whose error summary reports it.

FIXED. `audit.write` was unguarded, so a failing sink (read-only state directory, disk full, permissions) threw out of the setup path while producing no record at all. It is now caught and surfaced in the returned result — appended to the failure text, or carried as `error` alongside a successful install — so the operator learns the trail is incomplete instead of losing either the record or the result. Verified by a test whose audit write throws `EROFS`.

FIXED (security). The audit copy was redacted but the string returned as `error` was raw npm stderr, and that value is both shown to the operator and handed to the model as the command result — a registry token echoed by npm would have landed in model context. The returned text now goes through the same `redactText` as the audit copy. Verified by a test that feeds `_authToken=supersecret-token-value` through a failing install and asserts the result contains `[REDACTED]` and not the secret.

ADDRESSED IN PART, limitation stated. Deleting the drain used to keep the suite green because only the sink was tested. The drain-and-notify policy is now `reportDiscoveryDiagnostics` in the tested module (two new tests cover the count, the once-per-line contract and the silence of a clean scan), and the drain moved into a `finally` so a throwing verb handler still reports. What remains outside unit-test reach is the call site itself: the extension's command dispatch has no unit harness in this repository (the same limitation the Phase 1 review recorded for the engagement path), so the wiring rests on the packed smoke run. Reported as a limitation rather than claimed covered.

FOUND WHILE FIXING the others, and FIXED. `/devcontainer <verb>` produced no output at all: Pi's command dispatcher ignores a handler's return value (`_tryExecuteExtensionCommand` is `return await command.handler(args, ctx), true`, verified in the installed bundle) and nothing in the extension rendered `CommandResult.text`, so `list`, `status`, `logs` and the rest were silent even though the type documents the text as "Markdown rendered into the TUI". The dispatch now delivers the result through the same channel the handlers' own messages use; the policy half (`displayCommandResult`) is unit-tested, the wiring is smoke-covered. Not introduced by this phase and not part of its acceptance criteria, but it is the same defect family as the phase itself — output the code produces never reaching the operator.

FIXED. The shipped `README.zh-CN.md` documented `timeoutSeconds` without the new positive-value contract (the file is in `package.json` `files`, so the two READMEs disagreed in the published tarball), and `src/tool-output.ts` still described its parameter as "combined stdout (callers choose stdout-or-stderr precedence)", which became wrong when callers started passing `combineCommandOutput`'s result. Both corrected.

FIXED. Four assertions rewritten from the deleted registry fields into `expect(result.diagnostics).toEqual([])` asserted nothing about the removal and would have passed against the pre-change code. Three were deleted as redundant with the strong `entries` assertions directly above them; the fourth is kept, because a healthy scan reporting nothing is a real claim, and now says so and points at the registry-shape test that actually pins the field removal.

RESOLVED BY DOCUMENTATION. The diagnostics name host paths (unreadable directory, `maxDepth` pruning, a path that resolves outside the allowed root, a container without the Dev Container label). The disclosure is deliberate and bounded — operator UI only, never model context, never the audit file — and is now stated in `docs/troubleshooting.md` along with the once-per-session dedupe, so a future change that routes these into model context has to contradict the documentation rather than slip through.
FIXED. The drain ran after `await handler(...)`, so a throwing verb handler delayed its diagnostics by one command. It now runs in a `finally`, which is the property the new policy-level test pins.

CLOSED BY VERIFICATION. The host resolves `devcontainer` 0.89.0 while the repository pins and documents 0.88.0. Checked the installed 0.89.0 help output for every flag the adapter passes (`up`/`build`/`exec` with `--workspace-folder`, `--docker-path`, `--config`, `--container-id`, `--remote-env`): all still present, so the documented pin remains conservative rather than wrong and no documentation change is warranted.

RESOLVED. This was recorded as a blocking finding when the repair changed task-owned paths after the seal: approval for revision-078eb341 could not cover a tree it no longer described, and re-running verify reported all six acceptance criteria FAIL with repairScope `revision_superseded` — the documented "an owned file changed, build the next revision" signal rather than an acceptance failure. The repair was re-sealed as revision-99abdc7f and re-verified clean, which is why this finding is now a note. Kept instead of deleted because the sequence is the durable lesson: a review approval is bound to a revision id, so editing code after one is approved invalidates it even when the findings themselves are non-blocking.
